title: MatchTracker: silent fetchStats catch leaves users with blank state on API failure
notes: src/components/match-tracker/MatchTracker.tsx line 84: `catch { /* silent */ }` in fetchStats swallows all errors silently. When the /api/match-log GET fails (network error, 401, 500), loadingStats is cleared but logs/summary remain at their initial empty values and the user sees a blank stats panel with no indication of failure. Fix: surface a `loadError` state and render a user-visible error message. Note: the submit path (handleSubmit) does properly surface errors via setSubmitError — only the initial load fetch is silent.

title: Match log DELETE endpoint exists but MatchTracker UI has no delete button
notes: The DELETE handler exists in src/app/api/match-log/route.ts (lines 62-98) — it accepts ?id=<uuid>, verifies user ownership, and returns 204. However, the MatchTracker component has no UI to call it. Users who log a wrong result cannot delete it. Fix: add a delete icon button next to each log entry in the log list that calls DELETE /api/match-log?id=X and refreshes stats on success.

title: Champions meta SQL: Node.js aggregation instead of SQL — scalability cliff at 500 reports
notes: src/app/api/champions/meta/route.ts fetches up to 500 raw paste strings from the DB (LIMIT 500) and then parses + aggregates species usage in Node.js. This is a scalability cliff: at 500 reports, the code logs a warning and silently truncates the dataset, producing misleading usage percentages. Also transfers ~500 large text blobs from DB to Node per uncached request. Fix: push the COUNT/GROUP BY aggregation into SQL so only the top-N counts are transferred, removing the LIMIT-induced data truncation. The 5-min cache (CACHE_TTL=300) mitigates frequency but not correctness.
